## Summary

[[stripe]]'s overview of commercial off-the-shelf Tap to Pay readers for [[stripe-terminal]] names compatibility with the iOS, Android, and React Native SDKs. It links to a separate in-person acceptance route in the Dashboard App and to iPhone and Android setup guidance.

**Country availability in the overview tables**:

- **2026-11-07**: 39 iPhone markets and 40 Android markets. Both lists add Hong Kong (HK) and Mexico (MX) since May. Android also adds Japan (JP), which appears on both lists in November. Gibraltar (GI) remains the only Android-only entry.
- **2026-05-01**: 37 markets per platform. Japan appears only on the iPhone list and Gibraltar appears only on the Android list.

> [!note] Dated availability difference
> The 2026-04-24 [[source-stripe-terminal-regional|regional guide]] capture lists Japan for Tap to Pay on iPhone and omits it for Android, as does the 2026-05-01 readers overview. The 2026-11-07 readers overview lists Japan for both platforms. Use [[source-stripe-terminal-tap-to-pay|the separate setup guide]] for its dated GA and preview classifications and device requirements. The November table documents market listings. GA or preview status, account or device eligibility, and physical-reader availability require separate evidence.

**Updates**: Tap to Pay readers often initiate automatic software updates when they connect to the point of sale. The application needs to support these updates. Failing to install critical updates can prevent the reader from processing payments.

**Compliance as documented in both captures**:

- Apple completed MPoC (Mobile Payments on COTS) certification as a Monolithic Solution for Tap to Pay on iPhone.
- Stripe was undergoing MPoC evaluation for Tap to Pay on Android and linked to its MPoC Security Guidance.
- Before the PCI Security Standards Council released MPoC, Stripe completed security assessments directly with the major payment networks for network requirements applicable to Stripe. Stripe is described as a PCI Principal Participating Organization and a member of the PCI Board of Advisors.

terminal-tap-to-pay-readers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/tap-to-pay-readers, source-stripe-terminal-tap-to-pay-readers covers commercial off-the-shelf readers. The Dashboard App has an in-person acceptance route, and the overview names iOS, Android and React Native SDK compatibility (old raw lines 4-10 and new raw lines 5-11). The POS connection often prompts the reader to auto-update. The application needs to support that process, and a missed critical update can prevent the reader from processing payments (old raw lines 17-19 and new raw lines 18-20). Both captures say Apple completed iPhone MPoC Monolithic Solution certification and Stripe was undergoing Android MPoC evaluation, distinguish Stripe's earlier assessments with major networks before MPoC, and record Stripe's PCI roles (old raw lines 21-31 and new raw lines 22-32). The previous summary covered the same function but said SDK compatibility was exclusive and described update initiation and blocking categorically. Its JP exclusion for Android reflected the older list (old raw lines 12-15). The revised source restores compatibility and update wording and records that the November table places JP on both platforms (new raw lines 13-16).

GI remains Android-only and the sole difference in the November table, with 39 iPhone and 40 Android entries versus 37 per platform on 2026-05-01 (old raw lines 12-15 and new raw lines 13-16). The prior JP iPhone-only split is dated 2026-05-01 in the header of the file named 2025 (old raw lines 1-2 and new raw lines 1-3). Table formatting is presentational and the iPhone, Android, Dashboard App and MPoC Security Guidance links are stable navigation (old raw lines 8-15 and old raw line 27, new raw lines 9-16 and new raw line 28). The update and platform-specific compliance qualifications remain supported (old raw lines 17-31 and new raw lines 18-32). The Stripe index and company routes remain relevant, with the latter's 38-per-platform wording and undated Android Japan exclusion requiring correction. The stripe-terminal Regional Integration Rules gains a reciprocal reader-overview route and dates the earlier Japan split. The companion regional summary's undated Android-in-Japan exclusion (wiki/sources/source-stripe-terminal-regional.md:21-26) warrants separate qualification and routing. Its capture dated 2026-04-24 lists Japan for iPhone and omits Android there (raw/stripe-terminal-regional-2025.md:2,66), in agreement with the 2026-05-01 overview (old raw lines 14-15). The 2026-11-07 overview lists Japan on both platforms (new raw lines 15-16). The separate setup guide's GA and preview classifications apply to its 2026-04-24 capture. The November reader overview lists markets, and GA or preview status, account or device eligibility, and physical-reader availability require separate evidence.

concept_suggestions.anchor: **Reader availability exceptions**: DE = WisePOS E + S700 only (no S710); JP = S700 only (no WisePOS E, no S710, no Android Tap to Pay); GI = Tap to Pay Android only.
concept_suggestions.proposed_markdown: **Reader availability**: The 2026-04-24 [[source-stripe-terminal-regional|regional guide]] lists WisePOS E and S700 as smart readers for Germany and S700 for Japan. It also lists WisePad 3 as a mobile reader for both. That guide and the 2026-05-01 readers overview list Tap to Pay on iPhone for Japan and omit Android there. The 2026-11-07 [[source-stripe-terminal-tap-to-pay-readers|Tap to Pay reader overview]] lists Japan on both platforms and Gibraltar on Android alone. These rows document Tap to Pay market listings. GA or preview status, account or device eligibility, and physical-reader availability require separate evidence.
